html:
Nizar Qabbani was a Syrian poet and diplomat, born in Damascus in 1923, and the most widely read and sung Arab poet of his time.

He wrote about love and women's bodies in simple, everyday Arabic, which shocked many and won him millions of readers. Singers such as Umm Kulthum and Fairuz sang his poems. His sister's suicide, to avoid a forced marriage, made him a defender of women's freedom.

After the Arab defeat in the Six-Day War of 1967, he turned to politics, attacking Arab rulers in poems that were banned in many countries. He lived his last years in London and was buried in Damascus. See also Fairuz and Syria.
